target_model.text: The simulated GPIOA (factory/sim/stm32n6/gpio_model.py): Behavioural GPIOA model (RM0486 rev 4 chapter 15, feature 015) with the port A reset values: GPIO_MODER (0x00) 0xABFFEFFF, GPIO_OSPEEDR (0x08) 0x0C000000, GPIO_PUPDR (0x0C) 0x64000000, GPIO_SECCFGR (0x30) and GPIO_PRIVCFGR (0x34) 0x0000FFFF (F016 model gate: RM0486 reset values), the others 0. GPIO_BSRR (0x18, write-only) sets the GPIO_ODR (0x14) bits of BSy (bits 15:0) and clears those of BRy (bits 31:16), BSy winning when both are set; GPIO_BRR (0x28, write-only) clears GPIO_ODR bits. GPIO_IDR (0x10, read-only) reads GPIO_ODR back for pins in output (MODEy = 01) or alternate function (10) mode, 1 for input pins (00) with pull-up (PUPDy = 01) and 0 otherwise (pull-down, floating, analog). GPIO_OTYPER (0x04), GPIO_AFRL (0x20) and GPIO_AFRH (0x24) are storage. The lock sequence (GPIO_LCKR 0x1C), TrustZone, delay and advanced configuration registers are out of the work orders' scope: storage, not modelled. Expected values in target checks follow this model.

target_model.text: The simulated SPI1 (factory/sim/stm32n6/spi_model.py): Behavioural SPI1 model (RM0486 rev 4 chapter 67, feature 015), loopback master: SPI_CFG1 (0x008) and SPI_CFG2 (0x00C) are write-protected while SPI_CR1.SPE (bit 0) is set. Frames written to SPI_TXDR (0x020) wait in the TxFIFO (SPI_SR.TXC, bit 12, clears) until a master transfer runs: SPI_CR1.CSTART (bit 9), accepted only with SPE and SPI_CFG2.MASTER (bit 22), moves each frame to the RxFIFO (loopback: MISO = MOSI), setting SPI_SR.RXP (bit 0); after SPI_CR2.TSIZE frames (0 = endless) SPI_SR.EOT (bit 3) and TXTF (bit 4) are set, CSTART clears and TXC sets again. A read of SPI_RXDR (0x030) pops a frame (RXP clears when empty); a frame arriving with a full 16-frame RxFIFO is lost and sets SPI_SR.OVR (bit 6). SPI_SR (0x014) is read-only (reset 0x00001002: TXP, TXC); flags clear only by writing 1 to SPI_IFCR (0x018, write-only): EOTC bit 3, TXTFC bit 4, UDRC bit 5, OVRC bit 6, CRCEC bit 7, TIFREC bit 8, MODFC bit 9, SUSPC bit 11. SPI_CRCPOLY (0x040) resets to 0x107; SPI_TXCRC (0x044) and SPI_RXCRC (0x048) are read-only (0); other registers are storage. CRC, TI mode, I2S, interrupts, DMA and the half-duplex/simplex directions are out of the work orders' scope and not modelled. Expected values in target checks follow this model.

target_model.text: The simulated USART1 (factory/sim/stm32n6/usart_model.py): Behavioural USART1 model (RM0486 rev 4 chapter 65, feature 015), FIFO disabled, internal loopback (TX -> RX). USART_ISR (0x01C, read-only) resets to 0x000000C0 (TXE bit 7, TC bit 6). While USART_CR1.UE (bit 0) is set, writes to USART_CR2 (0x004), USART_BRR (0x00C), USART_PRESC (0x02C) and to the USART_CR1 fields RM0486 65.8.2 lets change only while disabled (FIFOEN 29, M1 28, DEAT 25:21, DEDT 20:16, OVER8 15, M0 12, WAKE 11, PCE 10, PS 9) are ignored. With UE set, ISR.TEACK (bit 21) follows CR1.TE (bit 3) and ISR.REACK (bit 22) follows CR1.RE (bit 2). A value written to USART_TDR (0x028) with UE and TE set is transmitted at once (TC set again, TXE stays set) and, with RE set, received into USART_RDR (0x024) setting ISR.RXNE (bit 5); a value arriving while RXNE is set is lost and sets ISR.ORE (bit 3). A read of USART_RDR clears RXNE. ISR flags clear only through USART_ICR (0x020, write-only, write 1): PECF 0, FECF 1, NECF 2, ORECF 3, IDLECF 4, TCCF 6; USART_RQR.RXFRQ (0x018 bit 3) discards the received value (RXNE clears). Other registers are storage. FIFO mode, interrupts, DMA, synchronous/smartcard/IrDA/LIN/RS-485 modes, auto baud rate and line errors are out of the work orders' scope and not modelled. Expected values in target checks follow this model.

target_model.text: The simulated TIM2 (factory/sim/stm32n6/tim_model.py): Behavioural TIM2 model (RM0486 rev 4 chapter 54, feature 015), 32-bit counter, internal clock only. Time advances by one kernel clock on every read of TIM_CNT (0x24) or TIM_SR (0x10) while TIM_CR1.CEN (bit 0) is set, so polling loops are deterministic. The counter steps every (prescaler + 1) clocks: up to TIM_ARR (0x2C) then 0 (DIR bit 4 = 0), down to 0 then TIM_ARR (DIR = 1), or up then down when TIM_CR1.CMS (bits 6:5) is not 0 (DIR then follows the counter). Each overflow/underflow is an update event (UEV): unless TIM_CR1.UDIS (bit 1) is set it sets TIM_SR.UIF (bit 0), loads the prescaler shadow from TIM_PSC (0x28) and, with TIM_CR1.ARPE (bit 7), the auto-reload shadow from TIM_ARR; in one-pulse mode (TIM_CR1.OPM, bit 3) it clears CEN. Without ARPE TIM_ARR takes effect at once. TIM_EGR.UG (0x14 bit 0) re-initialises the counter (0, or the auto-reload value down-counting) and the prescaler and, unless UDIS is set, loads the shadows and sets UIF unless TIM_CR1.URS (bit 2) is set. TIM_SR is rc_w0 (a written 0 clears a flag, 1 leaves it); TIM_EGR reads 0. TIM_ARR resets to 0xFFFFFFFF, the other registers to 0. Capture/compare, slave mode, encoder, DMA, interrupts and dithering are out of the work orders' scope: storage, not modelled. Expected values in target checks follow this model.
